title: Linear elasticity, nearly incompressible limits and locking

items.title: Algebraic gauge for a rigid-body stiffness nullspace
items.statement:
Let $K\in\mathbb R^{N\times N}$ be symmetric positive semidefinite, let $R\in\mathbb R^{N\times r}$ have full column rank and satisfy $\ker K=\operatorname{range}R$, and let $f\in\mathbb R^N$ be compatible in the sense $R^Tf=0$. Define the gauge solve as the procedure:

1. Form the square augmented matrix and right-hand side
$$
\begin{bmatrix}K&R\\R^T&0\end{bmatrix},\qquad \begin{bmatrix}f\\0\end{bmatrix}.
$$
2. Solve for $(u,\gamma)\in\mathbb R^N\times\mathbb R^r$.
3. Return $u$, which is the representative satisfying $R^Tu=0$.

The input hypotheses must be checked for the particular stiffness matrix. The procedure does not identify an omitted nullspace or assert a load is compatible.
items.strategy: Give the inputs, admissibility conditions, exact augmented system, and output; prove its algebraic properties separately.

references.title: Long Chen, Introduction to Linear Elasticity and Its Finite Element Approximation (complete 13-page notes)
references.locator: §1, printed pp. 1–2, and §5, printed p. 12: rigid motions do not change strain or stress and must be respected in discretization.

items.title: The rigid-body gauge system is nonsingular
items.statement: Let $K$ and $R$ satisfy the input hypotheses of [[alg-linear-elasticity-rigid-body-nullspace-gauge]]. Then $\begin{bmatrix}K&R\\R^T&0\end{bmatrix}$ is nonsingular. For $R^Tf=0$, its unique solution with right-hand side $\begin{bmatrix}f\\0\end{bmatrix}$ has $\gamma=0$ and is the unique $u$ satisfying $Ku=f$ and $R^Tu=0$.
items.strategy: Prove the homogeneous augmented system has only the zero solution, then use finite-dimensional rank-nullity and compatibility.

items.title: Linear isotropic elasticity: displacement form and data
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $d\in\{2,3\}$ and let $D\subset\mathbb R^d$ be nonempty, open, bounded, connected, and Lipschitz. Use the real spaces $V=H^1_0(D;\mathbb R^d)$ and $Q=L^2_0(D)$, norms $\|v\|_V=\|\nabla v\|_{L^2(D)}$ and $\|q\|_Q=\|q\|_{L^2(D)}$, and $b(v,q)=-\int_Dq\,\operatorname{div}v$ as in [[def-na-stokes-zero-mean-pressure-and-velocity-spaces]]. For a real normed space $X$, write $X'$ for its continuous real dual with operator norm $\|F\|_{X'}=\sup_{\|x\|_X\le1}|F(x)|$. Let $\mu\in L^\infty(D;\mathbb R)$ satisfy $0<\mu_0\le\mu(x)\le\mu_1<\infty$ almost everywhere, let $\lambda\ge0$ be a scalar, and let $f\in V'$. For any $w,z\in H^1(D;\mathbb R^d)$ define $\varepsilon(w)=(\nabla w+\nabla w^T)/2$ and
$$a_\mu(w,z)=2\int_D\mu\,\varepsilon(w):\varepsilon(z),\qquad \mathcal E_\lambda(w,z)=a_\mu(w,z)+\lambda\int_D\operatorname{div}w\,\operatorname{div}z,$$
and $\sigma_\lambda(w)=2\mu\varepsilon(w)+\lambda(\operatorname{div}w)I_d$. The homogeneous-Dirichlet model restricts these forms to $V$, with displacement zero on the full boundary; an example may prescribe a different boundary partition but gains no well-posedness claim from this definition. This is a linear small-strain model; no nonlinear, injectivity, or contrast-independent estimate is asserted.

Countable Choice is inherited through the imported Sobolev and Stokes-space conventions; this definition makes no arbitrary-index selection.
items.strategy: Give the typed model and exact coefficient, strain, stress, load, boundary, and norm conventions.

items.title: The mixed pressure has the mean-zero gauge
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $D\subset\mathbb R^d$ be bounded and open, let $0<\lambda<\infty$, and let $u\in H^1_0(D;\mathbb R^d)$. Since $D$ has finite measure, Hölder's inequality makes every $L^2(D)$ representative integrable, and almost-everywhere equal representatives have the same integral. Thus the local mean-zero space
$$Q_D:=\left\{q\in L^2(D;\mathbb R):\int_Dq=0\right\}.$$
Set $p=-\lambda\operatorname{div}u$. Then $p\in Q_D$. If additionally $d\in\{2,3\}$ and $D$ is nonempty, connected, and Lipschitz, this $Q_D$ is exactly the space $Q=L^2_0(D)$ of [[def-na-stokes-zero-mean-pressure-and-velocity-spaces]], so $p$ belongs to the mixed elasticity model's pressure space.
items.strategy: Use the zero-mean divergence supplier and closure of L2_0 under scalar multiplication.

items.title: Dirichlet elasticity energy bound and Galerkin estimate
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice and the data of [[def-linear-elasticity-displacement-formulation-and-data]]. For every finite $\lambda\ge0$ there is a unique $u\in V$ such that $\mathcal E_\lambda(u,v)=f(v)$ for every $v\in V$. It satisfies
$$
\|u\|_V\le\mu_0^{-1}\|f\|_{V'},\qquad \sqrt{\mathcal E_\lambda(u,u)}\le\mu_0^{-1/2}\|f\|_{V'}.
$$
For every finite-dimensional conforming subspace $V_h\subset V$, the Galerkin solution $u_h$ is unique and
$$
\|u-u_h\|_V\le\frac{2\mu_1+d\lambda}{\mu_0}\inf_{v_h\in V_h}\|u-v_h\|_V.
$$
items.strategy: Bound the form, use the homogeneous Korn identity for coercivity, apply Lax-Milgram, test with the solution, and apply the stated Céa theorem.

items.title: Displacement-pressure formulation and mini-element pair
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice, as in the imported model and mini-element spaces. Use the model, spaces, and sign convention of [[def-linear-elasticity-displacement-formulation-and-data]]. For finite $\lambda>0$, set $p=-\lambda\operatorname{div}u\in Q$ and write the mixed equations
$$
a_\mu(u,v)+b(v,p)=f(v),\qquad b(u,q)-\lambda^{-1}(p,q)_{L^2(D)}=0
$$
for all $v\in V$ and $q\in Q$. The pressure belongs to $Q$ by [[lem-linear-elasticity-mixed-pressure-gauge-is-well-defined]], which uses the zero-mean-divergence result. At the endpoint $\lambda=\infty$, define $\lambda^{-1}=0$ and impose $b(u,q)=0$; this is the incompressible constraint. At $\lambda=0$ use the primal displacement problem with $p=0$, not a mixed saddle system.

For a connected polygonal or polyhedral $D$ in dimension $d=2$ or $3$ with a conforming shape-regular affine simplicial mesh, the discrete pair $(V_h,Q_h)$ is exactly the P1-bubble/P1 mini-element pair of [[def-na-mini-element-p1-bubble-p1-spaces]]. The discrete mixed equations use the same $a_\mu,b,\lambda^{-1}$ and replace $V,Q$ by $V_h,Q_h$.
items.strategy: State the pressure sign, compressibility term, incompressible convention, finite-element spaces, and the separate lambda=0 branch.

items.title: Uniform mini-element stability through the incompressible limit
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice and the model and mixed conventions of [[def-linear-elasticity-displacement-formulation-and-data]] and [[def-linear-elasticity-near-incompressible-mixed-mini-pair]]. Let $D$ be bounded, connected, and Lipschitz, $d\in\{2,3\}$, $0<\mu_0\le\mu\le\mu_1$, and $f\in V'$. For every $\lambda\in[0,\infty]$ the continuous problem has a unique solution; at $\lambda=0$ use the primal problem and set $p_0=0$, while at $\lambda=\infty$ impose $\operatorname{div}u=0$. If $D$ is polygonal or polyhedral and $\{\mathcal T_h\}$ is any conforming shape-regular affine simplicial mesh family with a common shape-regularity bound, the mini-element discrete problem has a unique solution for every $h$ and every $\lambda\in[0,\infty]$, with $p_{h,0}=0$. There is a constant $C$ depending only on $d,D,\mu_0,\mu_1$ and the common shape-regularity bound, but independent of $\lambda$ and $h$, such that
$$\|u_\lambda\|_V+\|p_\lambda\|_Q\le C\|f\|_{V'},\qquad \|u_\lambda-u_{h,\lambda}\|_V+\|p_\lambda-p_{h,\lambda}\|_Q\le C\inf_{v_h\in V_h,\,q_h\in Q_h}\bigl(\|u_\lambda-v_h\|_V+\|p_\lambda-q_h\|_Q\bigr).$$
At $\lambda=\infty$ the constraint is $\operatorname{div}u=0$. The estimate makes no heterogeneous-coefficient robustness claim beyond the displayed dependence.
items.strategy: Separate the low-lambda projected primal branch from the high-lambda perturbed saddle branch; handle lambda=infinity by kernel coercivity and inf-sup, then prove uniform best-approximation bounds.

title: Linear elasticity, nearly incompressible limits and locking — Examples

items.title: Rigid motions in a free-body stiffness nullspace
items.statement: Let $D\subset\mathbb R^d$, $d\in\{2,3\}$, be a connected polygonal or polyhedral domain with a finite conforming affine simplicial mesh $\mathcal T_h$ and no essential boundary constraints. Define the continuous P1 vector space $S_h=\{v\in C^0(\overline D;\mathbb R^d):v|_K\text{ is affine for every }K\in\mathcal T_h\}$ and its global nodal basis $(\phi_i)_{i=1}^N$. For constants $\mu>0$ and $\lambda\ge0$, set $\varepsilon(v)=(\nabla v+\nabla v^T)/2$, $k(v,w)=2\mu\int_D\varepsilon(v):\varepsilon(w)+\lambda\int_D\operatorname{div}v\,\operatorname{div}w$, and $K_{ij}=k(\phi_j,\phi_i)$. For every infinitesimal rigid motion $r(x)=a+\Omega x$, with $a\in\mathbb R^d$ and $\Omega^T=-\Omega$, its nodal coefficient vector lies in $\ker K$. Thus the range of any complete nullspace basis supplied to [[alg-linear-elasticity-rigid-body-nullspace-gauge]] must contain these translation and rotation vectors. This example does not claim they exhaust the nullspace on every mesh.
items.strategy: Represent each rigid motion exactly in the continuous P1 space and evaluate its strain and divergence.

items.title: A manufactured shear field on a clamped rectangle
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice. On $D=(0,1)^2$, clamp the left edge $\Gamma_D=\{0\}\times(0,1)$ and prescribe traction on the other three open edges $\Gamma_N$. Let $\mu>0$ and $\lambda\ge0$ be constants and set $u(x,y)=(0,x)$. The stress $\sigma_\lambda(u)=2\mu\varepsilon(u)+\lambda(\operatorname{div}u)I_2$ is constant and satisfies $-\operatorname{div}\sigma_\lambda(u)=0$, $u|_{\Gamma_D}=0$, and $\sigma_\lambda(u)n=(0,\mu)$ on the right edge, $(\mu,0)$ on the top edge, and $(-\mu,0)$ on the bottom edge. This is a manufactured linear-elasticity solution; no uniqueness result for partial Dirichlet data is asserted.
items.strategy: Compute the affine gradient, symmetric strain, constant stress, and boundary tractions directly.

items.title: A fixed-mesh P1 volumetric-locking obstruction
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice. On $D=(0,1)^2$, let $c=(1/2,1/2)$ and split the square into the four triangles joining $c$ to consecutive corners. The continuous P1 vector space with zero boundary values has no nonzero elementwise divergence-free field. Choose a nonzero smooth compactly supported divergence-free displacement $u$ and set $f=-\operatorname{div}(2\varepsilon(u))$. Then $u$ solves the continuous model with $\mu=1$ for every finite $\lambda\ge0$, but the P1 displacement Galerkin solutions on this fixed mesh tend to zero as $\lambda\to\infty$, so their $V$-norm error tends to $\|u\|_V>0$. The mini mixed pair on the same mesh retains the $\lambda$-uniform best-approximation estimate of [[thm-nearly-incompressible-elasticity-mini-uniform-stability-and-error]]. This is a fixed-mesh obstruction, not a mesh-uniform P1 rate.
items.strategy: Compute all four element divergences, construct one smooth solenoidal exact solution, and use finite-dimensional compactness to prove the P1 discrete limit is zero.
